plan.description: Cerebrate produces the directive and delivery shape (single/multi/brood).

brood_confirm.description: Surface normalized strain task text for explicit user approval before dispatching the brood.

spawn_brood.description: Launch child overlord instances via the deterministic spawn substrate, then enter hatchery monitor mode.

git_preflight.description: Overlord verifies git state is safe before branch creation.

branch.description: Create or confirm the compliant working branch.

implement_next_step.description: Loop head: computes the ready set (a wave) of independent plan steps — depends_on satisfied and file scopes mutually disjoint — via the next-wave engine. Branches to implement_step (has_next_step) while any step remains, forward (all_steps_complete) when the done-set covers every step. One iteration is one wave, not one step.

implement_step.description: Overlord dispatches the whole ready wave as parallel agents (mixed drone/changeling from the static allowed set) in one batch, awaits all, then aggregates results with blocked > needs_replan > complete precedence. A wave of one step degrades to today's serial behavior.

checkpoint.description: Molt one checkpoint commit for the whole completed wave, not per step.

version_bump_decision.description: Overlord judges whether a version bump is required.

version_bump.description: Drone applies the version bump across artifacts.

version_checkpoint.description: Molt a checkpoint commit for the version bump.

validate.description: Overlord runs validation and judges pass/fail.

local_review_decision.description: Overlord decides whether local pre-PR review runs (Codex present and opted in) or is skipped.

local_review.description: Local reviewer runs the pre-PR adaptation cycle; reviewer-return outcomes are named transitions matching the local-reviewer exit_reason vocabulary. The reviewer's fix_commits_exist flag is surfaced for operator awareness only — it is a scalar field, not an exit_reason, so it is NOT a transition key and does NOT alter the deterministic route: 'clean' (and 'diminishing-returns') always target open_pr. The deterministic executor can only advance to the returned state. A post-review version re-evaluation, if the operator wants one when fix commits exist, is a separate user-initiated action outside this workflow's automatic routing.

review_remediation_plan.description: Cerebrate re-plans remediation when review escalates to the planner. Declares every cerebrate outcome (single|multi|brood|open_questions|blocked); a re-plan that yields steps routes to implementation, brood routes to the brood_confirm gate, open_questions/blocked surface to the user.

open_pr.description: Open the pull request for the completed plan.

github_review_decision.description: Overlord decides whether the post-PR watch loop runs. Watching is the DEFAULT and is opt-out only: the outcome is not_requested if and only if the user's original request carries an explicit instruction not to watch or monitor the PR; in every other case, including silence and ambiguity, the outcome is watch_requested. This rule is stated normatively in plugin/agents/overlord.md (the opt-out-only GitHub review watch default rule) — that agent rule is the source of truth and this description must stay in lockstep with it. There is no one-shot fix outcome here; an explicit user request for a single fix pass is served by the pr-feedback-remediation workflow's intake: fix route.

github_review_loop.description: Watch the PR and remediate review feedback until a terminal condition; reviewer-return outcomes are named transitions matching the github-review-loop terminal exit_reason vocabulary.

review_remediation_plan_postpr.description: Post-PR remediation re-plan: cerebrate re-plans when GitHub review escalates to the planner after the PR is open. Declares every cerebrate outcome (single|multi|brood|open_questions|blocked); a re-plan that yields steps routes to the post-PR implementation loop, open_questions/blocked surface to the user. The post-PR loop pushes remediation commits and re-enters the existing review loop — it never re-creates the PR. brood is BLOCKED in this post-PR context: a brood routes through brood_confirm -> spawn_brood -> hatchery_monitor (terminal), which would strand the already-open PR before it could reach validate_postpr -> push_remediation -> github_review_loop. Brood-shaped post-PR remediation must be surfaced to the user (matching pr-feedback-remediation's handling of brood in a post-PR context).

implement_next_step_postpr.description: Post-PR loop head: computes the ready set (a wave) of independent remediation steps — depends_on satisfied and file scopes mutually disjoint — via the next-wave engine. Branches to implement_step_postpr (has_next_step) while any step remains, forward (all_steps_complete) when the done-set covers every step. One iteration is one wave, not one step.

implement_step_postpr.description: Overlord dispatches the whole ready wave as parallel agents (mixed drone/changeling from the static allowed set) in one batch, awaits all, then aggregates results with blocked > needs_replan > complete precedence. A wave of one step degrades to today's serial behavior.

checkpoint_postpr.description: Molt one checkpoint commit for the whole completed wave, not per step.

validate_postpr.description: Overlord runs validation and judges pass/fail before pushing post-PR remediation commits.

push_remediation.description: Push the post-PR remediation commits to the working branch's remote (no PR creation) so the in-flight GitHub review loop resumes against the updated branch — the PR is never re-created.
